retained_source_profiles.structure: Contour stone lines for water harvesting and crop production
retained_source_profiles.conditions: Arid to semi-arid; agricultural soil, good local stone supply and slopes preferably below 2%.
retained_source_profiles.interpretation: The source expressly distinguishes these water-harvesting stone lines from stone bunding for hillside terracing.
retained_source_profiles.source_quote: Suitability Stone bunds for crop production can be used under the following conditions: Rainfall: 200 mm - 750 mm; from arid to semi-arid areas.

retained_source_profiles.locator: WOCAT PDF p. 129, printed p. 116, paragraph on contour forward-sloping bench terraces.
retained_source_profiles.conditions: Runoff is harvested from uncropped upslope inter-terrace areas. Catchment-to-application area ratio 1:1–10:1; slopes up to 60%; mainly for trees and bushes and less for field crops.
retained_source_profiles.interpretation: The published range describes where this design is used. It supplies no scores inside the range or exclusion threshold beyond it.
retained_source_profiles.source_quote: Contour forward sloping bench terraces are constructed or develop over time from vegetative strips, contour earth bunds and stone bunds on steeper slopes (up to 60%). This technology combines soil and water conservation with WH. Runoff is harvested from the sloping non cropped area between the terraces (C:A ratio 1:1 – 10:1). This type of terraces is used in areas with annual rainfall between 200- 600 mm/y

justification: Keep the Ronquillo seasonal model in its original regional context. Only the forward-sloping bench source supplies terrace-specific annual rainfall guidance. The contour stone-line source concerns a separate water-harvesting technique. No shared annual terrace rainfall score or cutoff is approved. Retained approved calibration hold; no new numeric synthesis or approval.

dataset_binding.reason: The asset has no Curve Number, runoff-depth or runoff-coefficient field. These are distinct input quantities; a new dataset cannot by itself validate the existing thresholds. A source-compatible input must be reviewed before use; the former HydroBASINS association and generic candidates are not approved substitutes.
dataset_binding.approval_scope: Dataset binding only; no evidence approval, numerical calibration or replacement dataset selection.

numerical_calibration.reason: The inherited opt_low=0.9 omits three ranked classes and assigns the optimum at a boundary the source specifies as strictly greater than 0.9. A class-preserving response requires reviewed endpoint and score conventions.

retained_source_profile.quantity: Modelled event direct runoff divided by design rainfall (Q/P)
retained_source_profile.input_method: SCS-CN; wet antecedent runoff condition III; 33%-exceedance probability of maximum daily rainfall used as design storm.
retained_source_profile.direction: Increasing suitability rank with increasing modelled event runoff coefficient for terraces and bunds in the source site-selection model.
retained_source_profile.boundary_ambiguity: Shared endpoints 0.3 and 0.6 are printed in adjacent ranges without an inclusion convention; >0.9 is explicit, and 0.9 is the printed upper edge of the highly suitable interval. Do not silently set .9 to optimum or infer interpolation.

importance.meaning: AHP source criterion weights, not calibrated response scores or approved runtime MCDA weights.

retained_source_profile.source_scope: Terraces and bunds, Ronquillo watershed, northern Peru. Existing EV and target mapping are terracing only; this proposal does not add bund-family applicability.
retained_source_profile.lineage: Source attributes boundary classes collectively to earlier manuals/studies; not independently estimated ecological transitions. Keep primary-source lineage unresolved rather than assign a specific cited source to the runoff classes.

justification: Peter approved the terracing calibration hold on 7 November 2026. Krois and Schulte (2014) ranked sites with four event-runoff coefficient classes. The reviewed source profile retains their class scores and AHP criterion weight of 0.14 for compatible synthesis. The former single-bound response and its uncertainty are archived with the decision. Dataset binding unresolved; requires matching input: The asset has no Curve Number, runoff-depth or runoff-coefficient field. These are distinct input quantities; a new dataset cannot by itself validate the existing thresholds. A source-compatible input must be reviewed before use; the former HydroBASINS association and generic candidates are not approved substitutes. Retained approved calibration hold; no new numeric synthesis or approval.
